parent.acceptance: accepted fixed-seed active three-position one-of-three RBD source

model.repair: unchanged half-hour direct system CM after return

manual_observation: Installed manual pp197 and 199-200,455-458 says nonoperated passive branches do not generate failures; a failed operated branch activates the highest-priority functional passive branch (lowest PRIO); positive TSWOV can place the block/system in SWITCHOVER. Manual pp199 and 456 describe activation failure timing differently, so no clock-onset claim is preaccepted.
hypotheses_to_test_natively: Both arms import/export/convert with zero errors and preserve exact B/A/C priority rows.
The first operated branch is POS-B, then POS-A is selected if B fails, then POS-C if A fails; native event evidence must identify branch selection rather than infer it solely from configured PRIO.
Nonoperated branches generate no failures before activation, consistent with the passive-state rule.
The positive-time arm spends an observable 0.5-hour interval in SWITCHOVER per completed switch and the zero-time arm does not; this is a hypothesis subject to native event and result-bin evidence.
Mission outcomes, failure samples, repair tasks and report bins are recorded separately for each arm; differing stochastic paths must not be described as identical draws.
acceptance_gates: frozen parent/source hashes, exact table delta, installed manual/dictionary/executable hashes
session-0 SSH with sshd ancestor, host-wide native mutex, preserved GUI PID 13340, unique run directories
native import/export/calc/report and exact authored-row roundtrip with zero converter errors
event-level branch activation, failure, SWITCHOVER, mission and repair reconciliation by author and independent read-only reviewer
raw invocation, logs, model, report and closure SHA-256 seals in evidence index
limits: One fixed seed and one repetition cannot establish population reliability or all standby priorities.

Fixed mission behavior may not generalize to continuous or extendable missions, online repair, all NBREQ bounds, unavailable preferred standby, overlapping switches, nested standby, GUI RBD views or cross-engine parity.
